target.title: fix(browser): detect Windows browsers when install roots are blank
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows browser auto-detection could miss standard Chrome, Edge, and Brave installations when LOCALAPPDATA or ProgramFiles environment entries were present but blank.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows install-root inputs are normalized at the browser plugin boundary before candidate paths are built. Blank values now behave like absent values, while nonblank custom roots retain their existing precedence.

## User Impact

Windows users can keep using browser auto-detection even when a launcher or service supplies blank install-root environment variables.

## Evidence

- Base behavior: the new production-entry regression failed with null instead of C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe.
- Exact head d7d2b3cf3a8a4c3c2cbfb2d362a401ab3977df1: focused regression -> 1 passed, 7 skipped.
- Command: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.default-browser.test.ts -- -t uses-standard-Windows-install-roots
- The test calls resolveBrowserExecutableForPlatform for win32 and only exposes the standard absolute Chrome path as existing, proving the real candidate resolver selects it.
- Targeted oxfmt check and git diff --check passed.



### Real Windows production proof

Ran the current PR head through resolveBrowserExecutableForPlatform on Windows with PATH empty and LOCALAPPDATA, ProgramFiles, and ProgramFiles(x86) blank.

Observed redacted output:

- blank-root detection: chrome at C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe
- real Playwright launch completed with installed Chrome 150.0.7871.125
- real page title round-trip: OpenClaw browser live proof
- after setting a nonblank ProgramFiles value of C:\Program Files, detection still selected the same installed Chrome path

This demonstrates both the blank-value fallback and preservation of meaningful nonblank root behavior on the current head.
